verdict_text:
NO

The plan omits one of the three mandatory checks: nothing asserts that exactly 64 tensors were merged. It asserts `count: 244` on `ft1`, `ft2` and on the final `base` namespace, and it asserts equality of the non-MLP tensors, but there is no `count ... is: 64` (or equivalent) over the MLP pattern, so if the regex matched a wrong number of MLP tensors — e.g. a typo silently matching only some layers, or the intermediate `tv1`/`tv2` set being incomplete — the run would still succeed. This violates the "Required checks" clause ("exactly 64 tensors were merged"). The rest of the plan is sound: both task vectors are formed against the unmodified base before either `add_`, lambda 0.4 is applied to each, the arithmetic is done in float32 and cast back to float16, the scratch `tv1`/`tv2` tensors are deleted, and non-MLP tensors are untouched.
note: experimenter: set `detected` (true if the stated problem matches expected_defect; for a correct artifact, true means a false alarm).
